findings.title: Module mixes five distinct concerns without separation
findings.description: synthesize.py (864 lines) conflates normalization, dedupe, evidence derivation, report building/validation, and serialization across 27 functions.
findings.remediation: Decompose into finding_processing / report_builder / report_validator / output_handler modules.

provenance.confirmation_reasoning: synthesize.py is 863 lines / 28 top-level defs and genuinely spans normalization, clustering, grading, assembly, validation, rendering, serialization and CLI. Caveats: evidence/citations/HTML are already delegated out, impact is purely maintainability, so HIGH is inflated (LOW/MEDIUM fits). CWE-1176 is misapplied; CWE-1080/1120 are correct.

findings.title: OS command injection via unsanitized shell script construction
findings.description: check_fixtures builds a shell script by f-string interpolating manifest paths into 'if [ -d "{p}" ]...' and runs it via sh -c. Paths containing shell metacharacters execute as commands.
findings.impact: An attacker able to modify tests/fixtures/manifest.json executes arbitrary commands in the container context.
findings.remediation: shlex.quote() the paths, or drop the shell entirely and pass a list argv (e.g. ['test','-d',p]).

provenance.confirmation_reasoning: Lines 52-58 interpolate manifest paths into 'if [ -d "{p}" ]' passed to sh -c; a path containing '"; id; #' escapes and executes. Sink is real and unsanitized. Severity caveat: the only source is a repo-committed file (attacker needs commit access) and execution lands in an ephemeral --rm container with no mounts. Remediation correct.

findings.title: Unescaped provenance.confirmation_status enables HTML attribute-injection XSS in generated reports
findings.description: _render_provenance interpolates provenance.confirmation_status into a single-quoted class attribute with only .lower()/.replace() applied, bypassing the module's _escape(). The value is agent-authored; normalize_finding never touches provenance and validate_report only checks the derived evidence.status. The report-schema enum on this field is never enforced (no jsonschema import anywhere in scripts/).
findings.impact: A prompt-injected reviewer can emit a confirmation_status that breaks out of the attribute, giving stored XSS in the HTML report when a developer or CI dashboard opens it. A non-string value also crashes report generation via AttributeError.
findings.remediation: Escape and coerce: _escape(re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9-]','-',str(status).lower())), or validate against the enum with a safe default. More broadly, actually enforce report-schema.json before rendering.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

findings.exploit_scenario: Injection payload in a reviewed diff manipulates the reviewer into emitting confirmation_status containing an img onerror; the payload executes when the HTML report is opened.

findings.title: Self-asserted source/reinforced fields let an agent finding forge tool_confirmed evidence and bypass advisor verification
findings.description: evidence.py deliberately ignores self-asserted provenance.confirmation_status, but is_tool_sourced() trusts finding['source'] — an ordinary JSON key the reviewing agent fully controls (its instructed field is source_role). derive_evidence returns tool_confirmed for it; build_verify_queue excludes tool-sourced AND reinforced findings from verification; normalize_finding/load_findings never strip either key; citations.enrich_citations also marks unrecognized CWEs verified:true for self-claimed tool sources.
findings.impact: A hallucinating or prompt-injected reviewer grants its own claim the pipeline's highest trust tier, skipping verification, becoming gate-eligible (able to fail CI on a clean change), and fabricating 'verified' citations — defeating the anti-self-assertion design via an unprotected equivalent field.
findings.remediation: Never derive trust from a field the payload can set: have load_findings pop 'source'/'reinforced' from agent-authored findings immediately after parsing, and let only ingest_tools and dedupe's real merge branches set them.
findings.exploit_scenario: An injected reviewer emits source:'tool:bandit' with severity CRITICAL on a harmless line; it is marked tool_confirmed, never verified, and fails CI with the authority of a real scanner.

findings.title: Unsanitized fixture paths interpolated into a sh -c shell script (command injection)
findings.description: check_fixtures f-string-interpolates manifest 'path' values into a combined shell script passed to docker run ... sh -c, with no shlex.quote. Any path containing a quote, backtick, $() or ; injects commands executed inside the fixtures container.
findings.impact: tests/fixtures/manifest.json is PR-modifiable; a malicious entry achieves arbitrary command execution in the container a maintainer or CI spins up.
findings.remediation: Run one argv-list docker invocation per fixture (no shell), or shlex.quote every path.

GitHub Actions step uses a mutable tag or branch reference. Tags and branch names can be silently repointed by the action owner, enabling supply-chain attacks — as seen in the trivy-action and kics-github-action compromises. Pin the reference to a full 40-character commit SHA instead, e.g. `uses: actions/checkout@8ade135a41bc03ea155e62e844d188df1ea18608`.

discarded_claims.title: Command injection via unescaped fixture paths in shell script construction
discarded_claims.description: check_fixtures builds a shell script by f-string interpolating manifest paths into 'if [ -d "{p}" ]...' and runs it via sh -c. Paths containing shell metacharacters execute as commands.
discarded_claims.impact: An attacker able to modify tests/fixtures/manifest.json executes arbitrary commands in the container context.
discarded_claims.remediation: shlex.quote() the paths, or drop the shell entirely and pass a list argv (e.g. ['test','-d',p]).

provenance.confirmation_reasoning: Pattern quoted accurately but no trust boundary is crossed: MANIFEST resolves to panopticon's OWN repo file, never a scan target; all four path values are static committed constants, never written by any code path. The precondition (attacker can modify manifest.json) already implies write access to run_fixture_tests.py itself, so injection grants zero extra capability. Dev-only harness; a shlex.quote hardening nit, not HIGH.
